questions.stem:
Statements:
Some monkey is dare
Only a few dare is amaze
All amaze is tall
Conclusions:
I. All monkey being amaze is a possibility
II. Some tall is dare
In this question below some statements are given followed by some conclusions. You have to take the
given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the
conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions definitely follows from the given statements,
disregarding commonly known facts. Give an answer.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
Source answer: (e) Both conclusions I and II follow

Only a few dare are amaze establishes some dare–amaze overlap. Since all amaze are tall, some tall are dare (II). No exclusion prevents all monkeys from lying within amaze, so I is also possible.

questions.stem:
How is Q related to K?
Study the following information carefully and answer the question given below:
There are nine family members: I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P , and Q. They belong to three generations.
K is the father of M and N. M is the sister - in - law of O. M is unmarried. J is the mother - in - law of O. L is the
father of O. I is the grandmother of Q. N is the father of Q. P is the sister of Q. Not more than five female
members in the family.
questions.explanation:
Source answer: (c) Grandson

K and J are the parents of M and N. M is unmarried; N is male and is married to O. L and I are O's parents. N and O have children Q and P; P is female. J, M, O, I and P already account for five females, so the limit of at most five females forces Q to be male. Q is K's grandson. M, N and O are the three second-generation members. If A is P's husband, O is A's mother-in-law.
